newsitem.title: UK: BA shares seen lower as results fall short.
newsitem.headline: BA shares seen lower as results fall short.

text.p: British Airways Plc shares were seen dropping some 20p to 30p in early trade on Monday after disappointing results from the UK flag carrier, dealers said.

The group posted a 46.7 percent rise in first-quarter pre-tax profit to 220 million stg, yet that total was boosted by a 130 million stg gain on the sale of its US Airways stake. Analyst expectations had ranged mostly between 115 million stg and 151 million.
"People just don't like the look of these figures," said one senior trader.
Operating profit fell 55 million stg to 140 million stg, dented by the strong pound, though underlying operating profits rose 5.6 percent.

BA said regulatory approval of its proposed alliance with American Airlines was proceeding very slowly and it was continuing to have talks with the UK Office of Fair Trading, the European Union's Competition Directorate and the U.S. Department of Justice.

It said the general business environment, including the start of a recovery in continental Europe, favoured growth in international air traffic though sterling strength would continue to depress profits.
